problem_statements.text:
In class, we discussed how to find the diameter of a tree using dynamic pro-
gramming. In this exercise, we will explore an alternative algorithm that solves
the problem using Breadth-First Search (BF S).
Describe an algorithm to find the diameter of a tree usingBF S.
Hint: prove that given any vertexwin the tree, at least one ofuorv(the
endpoints of the diameter) will be the vertex with the maximum distance from
w.

1. For the algorithmBF Sshown in class, answerT rue/F alsefor the fol-
lowing questions, and justify your answers. In every question,T BF S(G, v)
denotes the running time ofBF Son a graphGstarting from a node
v∈V(G). Assume|V(G)|=n.
(a) For every graphGand for everyv∈V(G),T BF S(G, v) =O(n 2).
(b) For everyn≥2, there exists a graphGovernvertices, and a vertex
vsuch thatT BF S(G, v) = Θ(nlog 2 n).
2. Recall the running time ofBF Son a connected graphGis Θ(|V|+|E|),
provided the graph is given in an adjacency list.
(a) Now the graph is still connected, but is represented as an adjacency
matrix. Give a tight bound for the running time of BFS.
(b) Give an example for a connected graphGand a vertexvsuch that

the running time ofBF Sis asymptotically different for the two ways to
represent the graph.
(c) Give an example for a connected graphGand a vertexvsuch that the
running time ofBF Sis asymptotically equal for the two ways to represent
the graph.
3. Answer the following questions and prove your answer.
(a) Give an example for a connected graph overnvertices, such that the
order of scanning the graph viaBF Sis always different than the order of
scanning viaDF S.
(b) Give an example for a connected graph overnvertices, such that the
order of scanning the graph viaBF Sis always the same as the order of
scanning viaDF S.
